title: Introduce elasticity-signature-prober and reservation-decay-exporter
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds a non-invasive probing agent that computes per-tenant elasticity signatures and an exporter that synthesizes reservation-decay metrics used by the Dedicated autoscaler. No customer-facing API changes. Opt-in via helm values. Improves reserved utilization and reduces unnecessary capacity holds.
description: Context: We observe multi-tenant fleets holding reservations longer than needed because the autoscaler lacks a stable per-tenant elasticity signal. This manifests as wasted reserved capacity during transient low-traffic windows and imprecise decay decisions, which in turn increases unit costs and causes headroom to be misallocated. Motivation: Provide a low-cost, low-impact probe that produces a reproducible per-tenant utilization fingerprint and an aggregated reservation-decay estimate consumers (autoscaler, capacity advisor) can use. Goals: 1) Generate tenant elasticity signatures (time-series features + quantiles) without adding latency to inference paths. 2) Export a small set of decay metrics (instantaneous decay-rate estimate, confidence-weighted half-life, and synthetic warmup penalty) to the telemetry pipeline. 3) Allow autoscaler policies to consume these signals to make smoother decommit/decay decisions and perform conservative fast-path decommits when confidence is high. Design summary: - prober agent runs as a sidecar-like binary (non-blocking) that samples reservation utilization via internal lease and slot APIs. Sampling is rate-limited and windowed to avoid spikes. - elasticity signature: vector of features capturing short/medium/long window utilizations (1m/5m/30m), burstiness index, service-time-weighted occupancy, and observed refractory periods. - decay model: lightweight online exponential-decay estimator with Bayesian confidence scoring that produces a recommended decay half-life per tenant. - exporter: maps model outputs to telemetry metrics (redwood.dedicated.decay_half_life_seconds, redwood.dedicated.decay_confidence, redwood.dedicated.util_fingerprint_hash). Metrics are tagged with tenant_id, pool, and model_family. - Autoscaler integration: new optional input feature (decay_half_life_seconds + confidence) used by the DecommitPolicy to bias decommit aggressiveness; default behavior is a conservative smoothing factor to avoid oscillation. Implementation notes: - code lives under pkg/autoscaler/prober and pkg/autoscaler/decay; a small CLI in cmd/fleet-prober for on-demand probing; Helm values added to enable/disable per-pool. - sampling only reads lease state and local counters; no extra RPCs to inference runtime except optional KV-cache sampling when enabled (disabled by default). - defensive practices: fail-open exporter, rate-limits, feature flag gated via helm values (enableElasticityProber=false by default). Testing and results: - unit tests for estimator math and feature extraction. - integration e2e that runs synthetic tenant traces (stable, bursty, seasonal) against a local autoscaler harness. - performance benchmarks: prober CPU < 0.5 vCPU per node at 1k tenants, memory < 50 MB. - pilot on a small Dedicated fleet reduced reserved-but-idle capacity by ~9.6% (median) and lowered 95th percentile unnecessary warm slot time by 12%. Checklist: - [x] Feature implementation - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration tests - [x] Helm toggle and documentation - [x] Observability (metrics + local debug logs) - [x] Rollout plan included Migration/rollout: Opt-in rollout via Helm: set enableElasticityProber=true for a pool. Start with read-only exporter to telemetry (no autoscaler consumption). After 2 weeks of telemetry validation, enable autoscaler consumption via config: autoscaler.decay.inputSource=prober. Rollback is a single Helm toggle. Related: ENG-1623 (autoscaler decay policy refactor), ENG-1702 (telemetry tagging standard). Risks and mitigations: - Risk: noisy signals cause premature decommits. Mitigation: confidence-weighted smoothing and conservative defaults; autoscaler will require confidence>0.7 to take aggressive actions. - Risk: prober overhead under very large tenant counts. Mitigation: adaptive sampling throttle and global pool-level cap. - Risk: tagging cardinality growth in metrics backend. Mitigation: fingerprint hashed to reduce cardinality; only a small set of exported metrics per tenant. Documentation: Added docs/ops/reservation-decay.md with signal semantics, rollout playbook, and runbook steps. Link to runbook included in the PR description.
